score.cap: grade limited to F: IPv4 INPUT accepts every new connection

findings.title: INPUT accepts new connections to any port
findings.detail: No rule refuses them, and the policy of filter/INPUT is ACCEPT. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.

fix.summary: Add rules for the traffic that is needed and test them, with a way back, then set the policy to DROP. The recommended baseline (--baseline) is a complete rule set to start from.

findings.title: 4 services are open to any source because INPUT accepts by default
findings.detail: No rule names their ports: A service on 8472/udp; sshd on 22/tcp; kubelet on 10250/tcp; kube-proxy on 10256/tcp. Close the default first; then accept each port that must stay reachable, for its clients only.

findings.title: FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule names
findings.detail: No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. The rules show that this host routes packets (address translation or Docker), so other hosts can send traffic through it to every network it reaches, including container and virtual networks.

fix.summary: Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.

findings.title: 2 forwarded ports are open to any source
findings.detail: nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 30080/tcp to 10.244.0.10:8080, 10.244.0.11:8080; IPv4 30443/tcp to 10.244.0.12:8443.

fix.summary: kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster. To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which sees the packet before the translation. The command below is for port 30080/tcp. For each of the other ports (30443/tcp), run it again with its protocol and its port.

steps.text: Drop port 30080 for all but the known clients, in front of the translation
steps.command: iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -p tcp -m tcp --dport 30080 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP

findings.title: Forwarded port 80/tcp of 203.0.113.50 is open to any source
findings.detail: nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 80/tcp of 203.0.113.50 to 10.244.0.10:8080, 10.244.0.11:8080.

fix.summary: kube-proxy writes this translation for a Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, and it writes its chains again all the time. Limit the Service in the cluster: set spec.loadBalancerSourceRanges, use a NetworkPolicy for the pods, or use type ClusterIP when the port needs no clients outside the cluster. To filter on the node, drop the port for other sources in the raw table, which sees the packet before the translation.

steps.text: Drop port 80 for all but the known clients, in front of the translation
steps.command: iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -d 203.0.113.50 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 ! -s <trusted-cidr> -j DROP

findings.title: OUTPUT default policy is ACCEPT
findings.detail: All outbound traffic is allowed. This is the usual setup; an OUTPUT allowlist can limit what a compromised service is able to reach.

notes.text: IPv4: 4 cluster IP addresses of Kubernetes services were not examined. A cluster IP is no address of the node; only hosts that route the service network through this node reach it.
No IPv6 rules were supplied: only IPv4 was analyzed, and IPv4 rules do not filter IPv6. Add the output of ip6tables-save as another file.

baseline.ipv4:
# Recommended IPv4 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (iptables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound traffic; outbound traffic is allowed. FORWARD keeps its
# policy: this host routes packets by rules that this file does not replace.
# Apply with "iptables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p icmp -m icmp --icmp-type 8 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Jumps of the present INPUT chain to chains that other programs manage.
# They are repeated here because INPUT is flushed. A chain that accepts
# traffic decides before the rules below: review what each one admits.
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m comment --comment "kubernetes load balancer firewall" -j KUBE-PROXY-FIREWALL
-A INPUT -m comment --comment "kubernetes health check service ports" -j KUBE-NODEPORTS
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m comment --comment "kubernetes externally-visible service portals" -j KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES
-A INPUT -j KUBE-FIREWALL
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Other listening services found on this host. Uncomment only what must be
# reachable, preferably with -s <trusted-cidr>:
# -A INPUT -p udp -m udp --dport 8472 -j ACCEPT   # unknown process
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10250 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kubelet
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10256 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kube-proxy
COMMIT
baseline.ipv6:
# Recommended IPv6 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (ip6tables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "ip6tables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Neighbor discovery is untracked by conntrack and must be allowed explicitly;
# a hop limit of 255 proves the sender is on-link.
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 134 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "router advertisement (SLAAC)" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 135 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor solicitation" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 136 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor advertisement" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 130 -m comment --comment "multicast listener query" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -d fe80::/10 -p udp -m udp --sport 547 --dport 546 -m comment --comment "DHCPv6 client" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s ::1/128 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 128 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh6-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
# Other listening services found on this host. Uncomment only what must be
# reachable, preferably with -s <trusted-cidr>:
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10250 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kubelet
# -A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 10256 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT   # kube-proxy
COMMIT
notes: SSH stays reachable on TCP port 22 (detected from the listening sshd).
Both families are always generated: IPv6 gets addresses automatically (SLAAC), so an unused stack must be closed too.
Keep a second SSH session open and apply with an automatic rollback, for example:
Persist the result with your distribution's mechanism (e.g. iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4 with iptables-persistent).

The baseline keeps the jumps of INPUT to chains of other programs (KUBE-PROXY-FIREWALL, KUBE-NODEPORTS, KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES, KUBE-FIREWALL). Rules in those chains are not part of the baseline: a chain that accepts traffic opens it whatever the baseline says.
IPv4 FORWARD keeps its policy (ACCEPT): this host routes packets, and the baseline does not replace its forwarding rules.
